newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice prices steady in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice prices steady in moderate trade.

text.p: Thai rice prices were mostly steady this week in moderate trade, trade sources said on Thursday.
China entered the market to buy top grade rice but in small quantities. Other orders came from regular cutomers such as Singapore and the United States, the sources told Reuters.
But demand for lower quality rice was subdued as some buyers were sidelined or turned to India for cheaper product while awaiting fresh supply from new crop to pull Thai rice prices down, they added.
Thai 100 percent B benchmark was quoted at about $330-350 per tonne FOB Bangkok while Thai 100 percent fragrant rice was quoted at around $610-615 on the same basis, barely changed from last week.
"There are some buying orders but nothing substantial," said one Thai trader.
"Demand for high quality rice is still good but markets for lower quality rice are a bit quiet," he said.
The Thai commerce ministry was upbeat about the rice tender results in Japan last week in which the country was expected to buy 35,800 tonnes of Thai rice.
"It is not a big amount but the trend is very encouraging," a foreign trade official said.

Under a 1993 General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade agreement, Japan agreed to gradually open its long-closed rice market and committed itself to importing 511,000 tonnes between April 1996 and next March.

"So far it held three rice tenders which accounted for about 155,300 tonnes this year. And we have the biggest market share of about 45.3 percent compared with 33 percent of the United States," the official said.
"This indicates a good trend. We expect that Thai exporters will be able to sell more rice to Japan for the remainder of import quota," she said.
Thailand exported about 4.28 million tonnes of rice between January 1-October 26, according to Thai Rice Mills Association.
